questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the incorrect statement.
options: $\mathrm{PEt}_3$ and $\mathrm{AsPh}_3$ as ligands can form $\mathrm{d} \pi$-d $\pi$ bond with transition metals
The $\mathrm{N}-\mathrm{N}$ single bond is as strong as the $\mathrm{P}-\mathrm{P}$ single bond
Nitrogen has unique ability to form $\mathrm{p} \pi-\mathrm{p} \pi$ multiple bonds with nitrogen, carbon and oxygen
Nitrogen cannot form $\mathrm{d} \pi-\mathrm{p} \pi$ bond as other heavier elements of its group
questions.solution:
- $\mathrm{PEt}_3$ and $\mathrm{AsPh}_3$ as ligands can form $\mathrm{d} \pi-\mathrm{d} \pi$ bond with transition metals.
- The $\mathrm{N}-\mathrm{N}$ single bond is weaker than the single $\mathrm{P}-\mathrm{P}$ bond because of high inter-electronic repulsion of the non-bonding electrons.
- Nitrogen has unique ability to form $p \pi-p \pi$ multiple bonds with itself, carbon and oxygen.
- Nitrogen cannot form $\mathrm{d} \pi-\mathrm{p} \pi$ bond as other heavier elements of its group.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the incorrect statement from the following :
options: Nitrogen can form $p\pi$-$p\pi$ multiple bonds with itself.
$\text{P}(\text{C}_2\text{H}_5)_3$ and $\text{As}(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5)_3$ form $d\pi$-$d\pi$ bond with transition metals.
Phosphorus, arsenic and antimony show catenation property.
Nitrogen can form $d\pi$-$p\pi$ bond with oxygen.
questions.solution:
Nitrogen and oxygen both belong to the second period of the periodic table.

The valence shell electronic configuration of nitrogen is $2s^{2} 2p^{3}$ and that of oxygen is $2s^{2} 2p^{4}$.

Since the principal quantum number is $n=2$ for both elements, they do not have vacant d-orbitals in their valence shells.

Therefore, nitrogen cannot form $d\pi$-$p\pi$ bonds with oxygen. They can only form $p\pi$-$p\pi$ multiple bonds.

Statement (1) is correct as nitrogen forms $p\pi$-$p\pi$ multiple bonds with itself (e.g., in $N_{2}$).

Statement (2) is correct because phosphorus and arsenic have vacant d-orbitals and can act as $\pi$-acceptor ligands, forming $d\pi$-$d\pi$ back-bonds with the filled d-orbitals of transition metals.

Statement (3) is correct as phosphorus, arsenic, and antimony exhibit the property of catenation.

Thus, the incorrect statement is (4).

Answer: Nitrogen can form $d\pi$-$p\pi$ bond with oxygen.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Match list-I with List-II :

List - I List - II
A. Coke I. Carbon atoms are sp3 hybridised
B. Diamond II. Used as dry lubricants
C. Fullerene III. Used as a reducing agent
D. Graphite IV. Cage like molecules

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
Coke when reacted with moderately reactive metal oxides at high temperature it forms CO and free metal during the metallurgical process. In this way coke play the role of removal of oxygen from metal oxide and hence act as reducing agent. 

In diamond each carbon atom undergoes sp3 hybridisation and linked to four other carbon atoms by using hybridised orbitals in tetrahedral fashion.

Fullerenes are the only pure form of carbon because they have smooth structure without having ‘dangling’ bonds. Fullerenes are cage like molecules. 

Graphite cleaves easily between the layers and, therefore, it is very soft and slippery. For this reason graphite is used as a dry lubricant in machines running at high temperature, where oil cannot be used as a lubricant.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Flourine is a stronger oxidising agent than chlorine because :
(a) F-F bond has a low enthalpy of dissociation.
(b) Flouride ion $\left(\mathrm{F}^{-}\right)$has high hydration enthalpy
(c) Electron gain enthalpy of flourine is less negative than chlorine.
(d) Flourine has a very small size.
Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given :
questions.solution:
Even though fluorine has lower electron gain enthalpy than chlorine, it is a strong oxidising agent. The correct reason that can be attributed for this behaviour is:
(i) Small size of fluorine, makes it suitable for its high hydration enthalpy.
(ii) The bond dissociation enthalpy of fluorine is lower than chlorine due to high lone pair lone pair repulsion.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Statement I: Acid strength increases in the order given as

HF<<HCl<<HBr<<HI

Statement II: As the size of the elements F, Cl, Br, I increases down the group, the bond strength of HF, HCl HBr and HI decreases and so the acid strength increases.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is false.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is true.
questions.solution:
Acidic strength of hydracids increases in order

HF≪HCl≪HBr≪HI

So, statement-I is true
The above order of acidic strength is due to decrease in bond strength. As the size of atom increases, bond length increases and bond strength decreases.
Thus, statement I and statement II are true

questions.q:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: The boiling point of hydrides of Group 16 elements follow the order
$\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}\gt\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{Te}\gt\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{Se}\gt\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{~S} \text {. }$
Statement II: On the basis of molecular mass, $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$ is expected to have lower boiling point than the other members of the group but due to the presence of extensive H -bonding in $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$, it has higher boiling point.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
questions.solution:
Statement I is correct, because boiling point of hydrides of group 16 follows the order
$\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}\gt\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{Te}\gt\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{Se}\gt\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{~S} \text {. }$
Statement II due to intermolecular H -bonding $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$ shows higher boiling point than respective hydrides of group 16.
(Both Statement are true)
Order from $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{Te}$ to $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{~S}$ is due to decreasing molar mass.

questions.q: The number of moles of hydrogen molecules required to produce <math><mn>20</mn></math> moles of ammonia through Haber’s process is:
questions.solution:
Haber’s process N2g+3H2g⇌2NH3g

According to the reaction,

2 moles of ammonia are produced from 3 moles of H2

i.e., 1 mole of ammonia is produced from 32 moles of H2

Thus, 20 moles of ammonia =32×20=30 moles of H2

Hence, 30 moles is the correct option.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Oxidation states of $\mathrm{P}$ in $\mathrm{H}_4 \mathrm{P}_2 \mathrm{O}_5, \mathrm{H}_4 \mathrm{P}_2 \mathrm{O}_6$, $\mathrm{H}_4 \mathrm{P}_2 \mathrm{O}_7$, are respectively
questions.solution:
Key Idea Oxidation state of $\mathrm{H}$ is +1 and that of $\mathrm{O}$ is -2.
Let the oxidation state of $\mathrm{P}$ in the given compounds is $\mathrm{x}$.
In $\mathrm{H}_4 \mathrm{P}_2 \mathrm{O}_5$,
$\begin{aligned}
(+1) \times 4+2 \times x+(-2) \times 5 & =0 \\
4+2 x-10 & =0 \\
2 x & =6 \\
\therefore x & =+3
\end{aligned}\begin{array}{l}
\text {In } \mathrm{H}_4 \mathrm{P}_2 \mathrm{O}_6, \\
(+1) \times 4+2 \times \mathrm{x}+(-2) \times 6 =0 \\
4+2 \mathrm{x}-12 =0 \\
2 \mathrm{x} =8 \\
\therefore \mathrm{x} =+4
\end{array}$
In $\mathrm{H}_4 \mathrm{P}_2 \mathrm{O}_7\begin{aligned}
(+1) \times 4+2 \times x+(-2) \times 7 & =0 \\
4+2 x-14 & =0 \\
2 x & =10 \\
\mathrm{x} & =+5
\end{aligned}$
Thus, the oxidation states of $\mathrm{P}$ in $\mathrm{H}_4 \mathrm{P}_2 \mathrm{O}_5$, $\mathrm{H}_4 \mathrm{P}_2 \mathrm{O}_6$ and $\mathrm{H}_4 \mathrm{P}_2 \mathrm{O}_7$ are $+3,+4$ and +5 respectively.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the correct relationship between the $\mathrm{pHs}$ of isomolars solution of sodium oxide $\left(\mathrm{pH}_1\right)$, sodium sulphide $\left(\mathrm{pH}_2\right)$, sodium selenide $\left(\mathrm{pH}_3\right)$ and sodium telluruide $\left(\mathrm{pH}_4\right)$ ?
questions.solution:
It is given that the isomolar solutions are sodium salt of Group 16 elements are present in equal molar concentration. The salts on hydrolysis with water, it produces an acid and base, as follows:
I. $\mathrm{Na}_2 \mathrm{O}+\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} \longrightarrow 2 \mathrm{NaOH}$
II. $\mathrm{Na}_2 \mathrm{~S}+\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} \longrightarrow 2 \mathrm{NaOH}+\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{~S}$
III. $\mathrm{Na}_2 \mathrm{Se}+\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} \longrightarrow 2 \mathrm{NaOH}+\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{Se}$
IV. $\mathrm{Na}_2 \mathrm{Te}+\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}\gt 2 \mathrm{NaOH}+\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{Te}$
The acidic strength of the hydrides is in the order $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} \lt  \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{~S} \lt  \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{Se} \lt  \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{Te}$, due to increase in the atomic size.
As the acidic character of the hydride increases down the group, the basic character of the salt decreases down the group. Therefore, the order of basic character of the salts will be: $\mathrm{Na}_2 \mathrm{O}\gt \mathrm{Na}_2 \mathrm{~S}\gt \mathrm{Na}_2 \mathrm{Se}\gt \mathrm{Na}_2 \mathrm{Te}$
Therefore, the order of $\mathrm{pH}$ of the given aqueous solution is $\mathrm{pH}_1\gt \mathrm{pH}_2\gt \mathrm{pH}_3\gt \mathrm{pH}_4$
Related Theory
The $\mathrm{pH}$ of the isomolar solution, can be determined with respect to the basic character of the sodium salts of the Group 16 elements. These salts undergo hydrolysis, forming hydrides, whose acidic character can account for the basic character of the salt, formed through neutralisation.
A Caution
In the reverse reaction of neutralisation, from the acidic strength of the hydrides, we can obtain the order of ease of neutralisation of the sodium hydroxide with the hydrides. As more the acidity of the hydride, more will be the neutralisation to form the salt.

Given below are two statements:
Statement-I : Heating NaCl with concentrated H_2$SO_4$ and MnO_2$ results in oxidation of Mn. \\ Statement-II : Heating NaI with concentrated H_2$SO_4$ and MnO_2$ results in reduction of Mn.
In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
The reaction of $\text{NaCl}$ with concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ and $\text{MnO}_2$ is given by:

$2\text{NaCl} + \text{MnO}_2 + 2\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 \rightarrow \text{Na}_2\text{SO}_4 + \text{MnSO}_4 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{Cl}_2$

In this reaction, the oxidation state of $\text{Mn}$ changes from $+4$ in $\text{MnO}_2$ to $+2$ in $\text{MnSO}_4$. Since the oxidation state decreases, $\text{Mn}$ undergoes reduction, not oxidation. Thus, Statement-I is incorrect.

The reaction of $\text{NaI}$ with concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ and $\text{MnO}_2$ is given by:

$2\text{NaI} + \text{MnO}_2 + 2\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 \rightarrow \text{Na}_2\text{SO}_4 + \text{MnSO}_4 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{I}_2$

Here, the oxidation state of $\text{Mn}$ also changes from $+4$ to $+2$, which means $\text{Mn}$ undergoes reduction. Thus, Statement-II is correct.

Therefore, Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct.

Answer: Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Assertion (A) $\mathrm{P}_4 \mathrm{O}_{10}$ cannot be used to remove moisture from ammonia gas. Reason (R) $\mathrm{P}_4 \mathrm{O}_{10}$ reacts with $\mathrm{NH}_3$ gas. The correct answer is
options: Both A and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both A and (R) are correct and (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{P}_4 \mathrm{O}_{10}$ can not be used to remove moisture from ammonia gas because it reacts with $\mathrm{NH}_3$.
$12 \mathrm{NH}_3+\mathrm{P}_4 \mathrm{O}_{10}+6 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} \rightarrow 4\left(\mathrm{NH}_4\right)_3 \mathrm{PO}_4$
Hence, Assertion and Reason both are correct and $(R)$ is the correct explanation of (A).

In laboratory, HCl is prepared by heating sodium chloride with concentrated sulphuric acid.

NaCl + H2SO4→420K  NaHSO4+HCl NaHSO4 + NaCl →823K  Na2SO4+HCl

HCl gas can be dried by passing through concentrated sulphuric acid as concentrated sulphuric acid being hygroscopic in nature as it  absorbs moisture from the air and gets diluted and acts as a drying agent. It has a strong affinity for water and thus it absorbs water quickly.

HCl reacts with NH3 and gives white fumes of NH4Cl.

NH3+HCl→NH4Cl

Assertion and reason are correct but the given reason is not the correct explanation of the assertion.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): VF5 is stable while VCl5 is not.
Reason (R) : Fluorine stabilises the higher oxidation state due to its higher bond enthalpy.
The correct option among the following is
options: <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></mfenced></math> is true, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi></mfenced></math> is true and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi></mfenced></math> is the correct explanation for <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></mfenced></math>

<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></mfenced></math> is true, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi></mfenced></math> is true but <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi></mfenced></math> is not the correct explanation for <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></mfenced></math>
questions.solution:
We know that fluorine atom can stabilise the higher oxidation state due to its higher melting point, higher bond enthalpy and small size and that is the reason with vanadium it forms VF5 whereas VCl5 is unstable due to the large size of chlorine atom such that there is no place of accommodation for five big chlorine atoms near the central metal vanadium and because of this stearic hindrance VCl5 does not exist in isolated form while it can exist in dimer form in solid phase.

Hence, assertion and reason both are true and reason is correct explanation of assertion

questions.subject: Chemistry

Given below are two statements :

Statement-I : Methane and steam passed over a heated Ni catalyst produces hydrogen gas.

Statement-II : Sodium nitrite reacts with NH4Cl to give H2O, N2 and   NaCl.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both the statements I and II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Both the statements I and II are correct
questions.solution:
In steam-methane reforming, methane reacts with steam under  3–25 bar pressure in the presence of a nickel catalyst to produce hydrogen, carbon monoxide, and a relatively small amount of carbon dioxide. Steam reforming is endothermic, that is, heat must be supplied to the process for the reaction to proceed.

NaNO2+NH4Cl→∆N2+NaCl+H2O

as NH4NO2→∆N2+H2O

Hence, both the statements are correct.

Statement (A) Sulphur vapour is paramagnetic is correct statement as sulphur vapour has formula $\mathrm{S}_2$, i.e. similar to $\mathrm{O}_2$ and $\mathrm{O}_2$ has two unpaired electrons in its anti-bonding molecular orbitals.
Statement (B) Reaction of $\mathrm{HCl}$ (dil.) with finely divided iron forms $\mathrm{FeCl}_3$ and $\mathrm{H}_2$ gas is a wrong statement as the whole reaction is as follows:
$\mathrm{Fe}+2 \mathrm{HCl}(\text { dil. }) \longrightarrow \mathrm{FeCl}_2+\mathrm{H}_2(g)$
The $\mathrm{H}_2(g)$ produced will prevent the formation of $\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}$ (i.e. $\mathrm{FeCl}_3$).
Hence, option (1) is the correct answer.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Observe the following statements :
a. The thermal stability of hydrides of group 16 elements follow the order :
$\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}\gt \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{~S}\gt \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{Se}\gt \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{Te}$
b. Acidic nature of hydrides of group 16 elements follow the order :
$\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}\gt \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{~S}\gt \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{Se}\gt \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{Te}$
c. The reducing nature of $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{~S}, \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{Se}$ and $\mathrm{H}_2$ Te follow the order :
$\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{~S} \lt  \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{Se} \lt  \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{Te}$
The correct statement are:
questions.solution:
- a. The thermal stability of hydrides of group 16 elements follows the order: \(\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} \gt  \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{~S} \gt  \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{Se} \gt  \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{Te}\) This is correct. As you go down the group, the central atom's size increases, and the E-H bond length increases. The bond becomes weaker and easier to break with heat, so thermal stability decreases.
- b. The acidic nature of hydrides of group 16 elements follows the order: \(\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} \gt  \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{~S} \gt  \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{Se} \gt  \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{Te}\) This is incorrect. The acidic nature increases down the group. As the E-H bond becomes weaker, it is easier to break, making it easier to donate a proton ( \(H^{+}\)). The correct order is \(\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} \lt  \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{~S} \lt  \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{Se} \lt  \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{Te}\).
- c. The reducing nature of \(\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{~S}, \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{Se}\), and \(\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{Te}\) follows the order: \(\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{~S} \lt  \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{Se} \lt  \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{Te}\) This is correct. The reducing nature increases as the E-H bond strength decreases down the group. It is easier for the hydride to donate hydrogen and get oxidized as the bond gets weaker.

questions.q:
Identify the correct statements from the following.
(i) Oxygen shows $-2,-1,+1$ and +2 oxidation states.
(ii) The thermal stability of $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}, \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{Se}$ and $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{~S}$ follows the order $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} \lt  \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{~S} \lt  \mathrm{H}_2$ Se.
(iii) The reducing nature of $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{Se}, \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{~S}$ and $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{Te}$ follows the order $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{~S} \lt  \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{Se} \lt  \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{Te}$
questions.solution:
Oxygen shows $-2,-1,+1$ and +2 oxidation states.
(i) Oxygen shows -2 oxidation states in most of its compound while it shows ( - 1) O.S. in peroxides (like $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}_2$ ), +1 in $\mathrm{O}_2 \mathrm{~F}_2$ and +2 in $\mathrm{OF}_2$.
Thus, it show $-2,-1,+1$ and +2 oxidation states.
(ii) The thermal stability of $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}, \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{Se}$ and $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{~S}$ follows the order $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}\gt \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{~S}\gt \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{Se}$ This is because, on going down the group, the size of the central atom increases and therefore, its tendency to form stable covalent bond with hydrogen decreases. As a result, the $M-\mathrm{H}$ bond strength decreases and therefore, thermal stability decreases.
iii) The reducing nature of $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{Se}, \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{~S}$ and $\mathrm{H}_2$ Te follows the order
$\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{~S} \lt  \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{Se} \lt  \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{Te}$

This is due to the decrease in thermal stability of the hydride greater the unstability of hydrides, the greater is its reducing character.

 In Etard reaction, chromyl chloride oxidises methyl group to a chromium complex, which on hydrolysis gives corresponding Benzaldehyde. The equation for the reaction is:

C6H5-CH3 + CrO2Cl2 →CS2 C6H5-CHOCrOHCl2 →H3O+ C6H5-CHO

(D) Gatterman-Koch reaction

When benzene or its derivative is treated with carbon monoxide and hydrogen chloride in the presence of anhydrous aluminium chloride or cuprous chloride, it gives Benzaldehyde or substituted Benzaldehyde. The equation for the reaction is:

C6H5-CH3 →Anh.AlCl3/CuClCO + HCl C6H5-CHO

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In the Ostwald process, the nitric oxide ($\mathrm{NO}$) gas formed in the final absorption tower is recycled back into the process.

Reason (R): Aqueous nitric acid obtained by the absorption of $\mathrm{NO}_2$ in water can be concentrated to $98\%$ by mass using simple distillation.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is correct. In the final step of the Ostwald process, nitrogen dioxide is absorbed in water to form nitric acid and nitric oxide:
$3\mathrm{NO}_2(\mathrm{g}) + \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}(\mathrm{l}) \rightarrow 2\mathrm{HNO}_3(\mathrm{aq}) + \mathrm{NO}(\mathrm{g})$
The $\mathrm{NO}$ gas thus formed is recycled and re-oxidised to $\mathrm{NO}_2$.

Reason (R) is incorrect. Aqueous nitric acid obtained by this method can be concentrated by distillation only up to $\sim 68\%$ by mass, as it forms a constant boiling mixture (azeotrope) with water. Further concentration to $98\%$ requires dehydration with concentrated $\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{SO}_4$.

Answer: (A) is correct but (R) is not correct

The balanced chemical equation for the catalytic oxidation of ammonia in the Ostwald process is:
$4NH_{3}(g) + 5O_{2}(g) \rightarrow 4NO(g) + 6H_{2}O(g)$

According to the stoichiometry of the reaction, $4$ moles of $NO$ are produced by the reaction of $5$ moles of $O_{2}$.

Therefore, $1$ mole of $NO$ requires $\dfrac{5}{4}$ moles of $O_{2}$.

To produce $20$ moles of $NO$, the number of moles of $O_{2}$ required is:
Moles of $O_{2} = \dfrac{5}{4} \times 20 = 25$ moles.

Thus, $25$ moles of oxygen gas are required.

Answer: $25$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Chlorine, bromine, and iodine can be prepared by heating their respective metal halides with Mn$O_2$ and concentrated H_2$SO_4$. However, fluorine ($F_2$) cannot be prepared from fluorides (such as Ca$F_2$) using this method. What is the primary chemical reason for this?
options: F_2$ reacts violently with H_2$SO_4$ to form explosive compounds.$
MnO_2$ is a weaker oxidizing agent than F_2$ and cannot oxidize F$^-$ ions.
Mn$O_2$ acts as a reducing agent in the presence of fluorides.
CaF_2$ is completely insoluble in concentrated H_2$SO_4$.$
questions.solution: The preparation of halogens using Mn$O_2$ and concentrated H_2$SO_4$ is a redox reaction where MnO_2$ acts as an oxidizing agent, oxidizing the halide ions (Cl$^-$, Br$^-$, I$^-$) to their respective halogens (Cl_2$, Br_2$, I_2$). \\  \\ Fluorine ($F_2$) is the strongest chemical oxidizing agent known. Its standard reduction potential is much higher than that of MnO_2$. Therefore, MnO_2$ does not possess sufficient oxidizing power to oxidize fluoride ions (F$^-$) to fluorine gas ($F_2$). \\  \\ Thus, the reaction fails because MnO_2$ is a weaker oxidizing agent than $F_2$. \\  \\ Answer: MnO_2$ is a weaker oxidizing agent than $F_2$ and cannot oxidize F$^-$ ions.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Read the following statements carefully:

Statement I: $\text{XeF}_2$ is a linear molecule with three lone pairs of electrons at equatorial positions.
Statement II: $\text{ClF}_3$ has a T-shape with two lone pairs of electrons at axial positions.
Statement III: $\text{XeF}_6$ has a distorted octahedral shape and $\text{sp}^3\text{d}^3$ hybridization.
Statement IV: $\text{BrF}_5$ has a square planar geometry with one lone pair.

How many of the given statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement I is correct: In $\text{XeF}_2$, the central Xe atom has 8 valence electrons. It forms 2 single bonds with F atoms, leaving 3 lone pairs. The hybridization is $\text{sp}^3\text{d}$. To minimize repulsion, the three lone pairs occupy the equatorial positions, resulting in a linear shape.

Statement II is incorrect: In $\text{ClF}_3$, the central Cl atom is $\text{sp}^3\text{d}$ hybridized with 3 bond pairs and 2 lone pairs. The lone pairs occupy equatorial positions (not axial) to minimize lone pair-lone pair repulsions, giving it a T-shape.

Statement III is correct: In $\text{XeF}_6$, Xe has 6 bond pairs and 1 lone pair. The hybridization is $\text{sp}^3\text{d}^3$, and the shape is distorted octahedral.

Statement IV is incorrect: In $\text{BrF}_5$, Br has 5 bond pairs and 1 lone pair. The hybridization is $\text{sp}^3\text{d}^2$, which corresponds to a square pyramidal geometry, not square planar.

Therefore, only two statements (I and III) are correct.

Answer: Only two

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Buckminsterfullerene ($\text{C}_{60}$):
(a) It contains 20 six-membered rings and 12 five-membered rings.
(b) All carbon atoms in it undergo $\text{sp}^{2}$ hybridization.
(c) It is the only pure form of carbon because it has a smooth structure without dangling bonds.
(d) Six-membered rings are fused only to other six-membered rings, while five-membered rings are fused to both five and six-membered rings.

How many of the given statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement (a) is correct: Buckminsterfullerene ($\text{C}_{60}$) consists of 20 six-membered rings and 12 five-membered rings.

Statement (b) is correct: All carbon atoms in $\text{C}_{60}$ are equivalent and undergo $\text{sp}^{2}$ hybridization.

Statement (c) is correct: Fullerenes are the only pure form of carbon because they have a smooth, closed cage structure without any dangling bonds.

Statement (d) is incorrect: According to NCERT, a six-membered ring can fuse with both six-membered and five-membered rings, whereas a five-membered ring can only fuse with six-membered rings.

Therefore, exactly 3 statements are correct.

Answer: 3

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Three Xenon compounds A, B, and C have square planar, linear, and square pyramidal geometries respectively. The number of lone pairs on the central Xenon atom in compounds A, B, and C are respectively:
questions.solution:
For a Xenon compound to have a square planar geometry (e.g., $\text{XeF}_4$), the central Xe atom undergoes $sp^3d^2$ hybridization with 4 bond pairs and 2 lone pairs.

For a linear geometry (e.g., $\text{XeF}_2$), the central Xe atom undergoes $sp^3d$ hybridization with 2 bond pairs and 3 lone pairs.

For a square pyramidal geometry (e.g., $\text{XeOF}_4$), the central Xe atom undergoes $sp^3d^2$ hybridization with 5 bond pairs and 1 lone pair.

Therefore, the number of lone pairs on the central Xenon atom in compounds A, B, and C are 2, 3, and 1 respectively.

Answer: 2, 3, 1

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: If $10\text{ moles}$ of dinitrogen and $15\text{ moles}$ of dihydrogen are mixed in a closed vessel to synthesize ammonia, what is the maximum number of moles of ammonia that can be formed?
questions.solution:
The balanced chemical equation for the synthesis of ammonia is:

$\text{N}_{2}(\text{g}) + 3\text{H}_{2}(\text{g}) \rightleftharpoons 2\text{NH}_{3}(\text{g})$

According to the reaction, $1\text{ mole}$ of $\text{N}_{2}$ requires $3\text{ moles}$ of $\text{H}_{2}$.
For $10\text{ moles}$ of $\text{N}_{2}$, the required moles of $\text{H}_{2} = 10 \times 3 = 30\text{ moles}$.
Since only $15\text{ moles}$ of $\text{H}_{2}$ are available, $\text{H}_{2}$ is the limiting reagent.

The amount of product formed depends on the limiting reagent.
From the balanced equation, $3\text{ moles}$ of $\text{H}_{2}$ produce $2\text{ moles}$ of $\text{NH}_{3}$.
Therefore, $15\text{ moles}$ of $\text{H}_{2}$ will produce $\dfrac{2}{3} \times 15 = 10\text{ moles}$ of $\text{NH}_{3}$.

Answer: $10$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Match the reactants or stages of the Ostwald process given in List-I with their corresponding catalysts, conditions, or products given in List-II.

List-IList-II
(A) $\mathrm{NH_3} + \mathrm{O_2}$(I) Recycled $\mathrm{NO}$ gas
(B) $\mathrm{NO} + \mathrm{O_2}$(II) $\mathrm{Pt}/\mathrm{Rh}$ gauge catalyst at $500 \mathrm{~K}$
(C) $\mathrm{NO_2} + \mathrm{H_2O}$(III) Concentrated $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$
(D) Aqueous $\mathrm{HNO_3}$ ($\sim 68\%$ by mass)(IV) $\mathrm{NO_2}$ gas

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
The Ostwald process involves the following sequential steps and conditions:

(A) The first step is the catalytic oxidation of ammonia by atmospheric oxygen. This reaction requires a $\mathrm{Pt}/\mathrm{Rh}$ gauge catalyst at $500 \mathrm{~K}$ and $9 \text{ bar}$ pressure. Hence, (A) matches with (II).

(B) The second step is the oxidation of nitric oxide ($\mathrm{NO}$) to nitrogen dioxide ($\mathrm{NO_2}$) gas. Hence, (B) matches with (IV).

(C) The third step is the absorption of $\mathrm{NO_2}$ in water to form aqueous $\mathrm{HNO_3}$ and a byproduct, $\mathrm{NO}$ gas, which is recycled. Hence, (C) matches with (I).

(D) The aqueous $\mathrm{HNO_3}$ obtained is concentrated by distillation up to $\sim 68\%$ by mass. Further concentration to $98\%$ is achieved by dehydration using concentrated $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$. Hence, (D) matches with (III).

Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(II), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(III).

Answer: (A)-(II), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(III)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A): Nitrogen forms $\text{N}_2\text{O}_5$ but does not form $\text{NCl}_5$.
Reason (R): Nitrogen lacks vacant d-orbitals in its valence shell, restricting its maximum covalency to 4.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is true: Nitrogen forms the pentoxide $\text{N}_2\text{O}_5$ but cannot form the pentahalide $\text{NCl}_5$.

Reason (R) is true and correctly explains (A): Nitrogen has only one s and three p orbitals in its valence shell, so its maximum covalency is restricted to 4. In $\text{N}_2\text{O}_5$, nitrogen exhibits a +5 oxidation state but its covalency does not exceed 4. However, to form $\text{NCl}_5$, nitrogen would need to form five single bonds, requiring a covalency of 5. Since it lacks vacant d-orbitals to expand its octet, $\text{NCl}_5$ does not exist.

Answer: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the pair of species in which the first species contains exclusively $p\pi$-$p\pi$ multiple bonds and the second species contains $d\pi$-$p\pi$ multiple bonds.
questions.solution:
Nitrogen belongs to the second period and its valence shell configuration is $2s^2 2p^3$. Since it lacks vacant d-orbitals, it can only form $p\pi$-$p\pi$ multiple bonds (e.g., in $\text{N}_2$, $\text{NO}_2^-$, $\text{NO}_3^-$).

Phosphorus and sulphur belong to the third period and have vacant d-orbitals in their valence shells. Thus, they can form $d\pi$-$p\pi$ multiple bonds with oxygen (e.g., in $\text{PO}_4^{3-}$, $\text{SO}_4^{2-}$).

In the given options, $\text{NO}_3^-$ contains exclusively $p\pi$-$p\pi$ bonds, while $\text{PO}_4^{3-}$ contains $d\pi$-$p\pi$ bonds. Therefore, the correct pair is $\text{NO}_3^-$ and $\text{PO}_4^{3-}$.

Answer: $\text{NO}_3^-$ and $\text{PO}_4^{3-}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the hydrides of Group 17 elements:
(I) The thermal stability of the hydrides follows the order $\mathrm{HF} \gt \mathrm{HCl} \gt \mathrm{HBr} \gt \mathrm{HI}$.
(II) The reducing power of the hydrides follows the order $\mathrm{HF} \lt \mathrm{HCl} \lt \mathrm{HBr} \lt \mathrm{HI}$.
(III) The boiling points of the hydrides follow the order $\mathrm{HCl} \lt \mathrm{HBr} \lt \mathrm{HI} \lt \mathrm{HF}$.
(IV) The acidic strength of the hydrides follows the order $\mathrm{HI} \gt \mathrm{HBr} \gt \mathrm{HCl} \gt \mathrm{HF}$.

How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement (I) is correct: Thermal stability decreases down the group as the $\mathrm{H-X}$ bond dissociation enthalpy decreases from $\mathrm{HF}$ to $\mathrm{HI}$.

Statement (II) is correct: Reducing power increases down the group because the decreasing bond enthalpy makes it easier to release hydrogen.

Statement (III) is correct: $\mathrm{HF}$ has an anomalously high boiling point due to strong intermolecular hydrogen bonding. For the other hydrogen halides, the boiling point increases with molecular mass due to increasing magnitude of van der Waals forces.

Statement (IV) is correct: Acidic strength increases down the group as the $\mathrm{H-X}$ bond becomes weaker and easier to break in aqueous solution.

Therefore, all four statements are correct.

Answer: Four

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the incorrect statement regarding the elements of Group 16.
options: The $\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{O}$ single bond is stronger than the $\mathrm{S}-\mathrm{S}$ single bond.
Oxygen shows a much lower tendency for catenation than sulphur.
Sulphur can form $\mathrm{d} \pi-\mathrm{p} \pi$ multiple bonds whereas oxygen cannot.
Oxygen cannot expand its covalency beyond four due to the absence of d-orbitals.
questions.solution:
The $\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{O}$ single bond is weaker than the $\mathrm{S}-\mathrm{S}$ single bond because of high interelectronic repulsion between the lone pairs of electrons on the small oxygen atoms. Thus, the statement claiming it is stronger is incorrect.

Due to the weaker $\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{O}$ single bond, oxygen has a much lower tendency for catenation compared to sulphur.

Sulphur has vacant d-orbitals and can form $\mathrm{d} \pi-\mathrm{p} \pi$ multiple bonds, while oxygen is restricted to $\mathrm{p} \pi-\mathrm{p} \pi$ bonding due to the absence of d-orbitals.

The absence of d-orbitals in the valence shell of oxygen limits its covalency to a maximum of four.

Answer: The $\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{O}$ single bond is stronger than the $\mathrm{S}-\mathrm{S}$ single bond.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the preparation of some p-block elements and their compounds:
(A) Pure nitrogen is obtained by the thermal decomposition of barium azide.
(B) In the Haber process, iron oxide with small amounts of $\text{K}_2\text{O}$ and $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ is used as a catalyst.
(C) The Contact process involves the oxidation of $\text{SO}_2$ to $\text{SO}_3$ using $\text{CuCl}_2$ as a catalyst.
(D) Deacon's process is used for the commercial preparation of chlorine gas.

How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement (A) is correct as very pure nitrogen is obtained by the thermal decomposition of sodium or barium azide.

Statement (B) is correct; iron oxide with small amounts of $\text{K}_2\text{O}$ and $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ is the catalyst currently used in the Haber process for the manufacture of ammonia.

Statement (C) is incorrect because the oxidation of $\text{SO}_2$ to $\text{SO}_3$ in the Contact process uses $\text{V}_2\text{O}_5$ as a catalyst. $\text{CuCl}_2$ is used as a catalyst in Deacon's process.

Statement (D) is correct; Deacon's process is a commercial method for preparing chlorine gas by the oxidation of $\text{HCl}$ gas.

Thus, exactly three statements are correct.

Answer: Three

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Reagents)List-II (Observation)
(A) NaCl + conc. $H_2$SO_4$(I) Greenish-yellow gas
(B) NaCl + MnO_2$ + conc. H_2$SO_4$(II) Reddish-brown gas
(C) NaBr + MnO_2$ + conc. H_2$SO_4$(III) Violet vapors
(D) NaI + MnO_2$ + conc. H_2$SO_4$(IV) Colorless pungent gas


Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
When NaCl is heated with concentrated $H_2$SO_4$, hydrogen chloride (HCl) gas is evolved, which is a colorless gas with a pungent odor. Thus, (A) matches (IV).

When NaCl is heated with MnO_2$ and concentrated H_2$SO_4$, MnO_2$ acts as an oxidizing agent and oxidizes the chloride ions to chlorine (Cl_2$) gas, which is a greenish-yellow gas. Thus, (B) matches (I). \\ \\ Similarly, heating NaBr with MnO_2$ and concentrated H_2$SO_4$ produces bromine (Br_2$) gas, which evolves as reddish-brown vapors. Thus, (C) matches (II). \\ \\ Heating NaI with MnO_2$ and concentrated H_2$SO_4$ produces iodine (I_2$), which evolves as violet vapors. Thus, (D) matches (III).

Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(IV), (B)-(I), (C)-(II), (D)-(III).

Answer: (A)-(IV), (B)-(I), (C)-(II), (D)-(III)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Consider the following catalytic step used in an industrial manufacturing process:

$2SO_2(g) + O_2(g) \xrightarrow{V_2O_5} 2SO_3(g)$

Identify the name of the industrial process to which this step belongs, and the thermodynamic nature of this specific reaction.
questions.solution:
The given reaction is the key catalytic step in the Contact process for the manufacture of sulphuric acid.

In this step, sulphur dioxide is oxidized to sulphur trioxide in the presence of vanadium(V) oxide ($V_2O_5$) catalyst.

The reaction is highly exothermic ($\Delta_r H^{\ominus} = -196.6 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$) and reversible. Therefore, low temperature and high pressure are the favourable conditions for maximum yield, though the temperature must be high enough for the catalyst to be effective.

Answer: Contact process, Exothermic

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Match List I with List II:

List IList II
(A) $\mathrm{HNO_2}$(I) Strongest reducing agent among group 15 hydrides
(B) $\mathrm{BiH_3}$(II) Undergoes disproportionation in acidic medium
(C) $\mathrm{N_2O_5}$(III) +3 oxidation state is more stable than +5
(D) Bismuth(IV) Most acidic oxide among group 15

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
(A) $\mathrm{HNO_2}$ undergoes disproportionation in an acidic medium to form $\mathrm{HNO_3}$ and $\mathrm{NO}$.

(B) $\mathrm{BiH_3}$ is the strongest reducing agent among Group 15 hydrides because the E-H bond dissociation enthalpy decreases down the group.

(C) $\mathrm{N_2O_5}$ is the most acidic oxide among Group 15 elements, as acidic character of oxides decreases down the group.

(D) For Bismuth, the +3 oxidation state is much more stable than the +5 oxidation state due to the prominent inert pair effect.

Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(II), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(III).

Answer: (A)-(II), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(III)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Gas X is produced commercially by Deacon's process. When gas X reacts with dry slaked lime, it gives a compound Y which is widely used as a bleaching agent.

Identify gas X and the active bleaching ion present in compound Y.
questions.solution:
Gas X is chlorine ($\text{Cl}_2$), which is manufactured commercially by Deacon's process. This process involves the oxidation of hydrogen chloride gas by atmospheric oxygen in the presence of a $\text{CuCl}_2$ catalyst.

Chlorine reacts with dry slaked lime ($\text{Ca(OH)}_2$) to produce bleaching powder. The reaction is:
$2\text{Ca(OH)}_2 + 2\text{Cl}_2 \rightarrow \text{Ca(OCl)}_2 + \text{CaCl}_2 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$

The composition of bleaching powder is represented as $\text{Ca(OCl)}_2 \cdot \text{CaCl}_2 \cdot \text{Ca(OH)}_2 \cdot 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$. The active bleaching agent in it is the hypochlorite ion ($\text{ClO}^-$ or $\text{OCl}^-$).

Answer: $\text{Cl}_2$ and $\text{ClO}^-$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Match List I with List II regarding the properties of Group 16 hydrides ($\text{H}_2\text{O}$, $\text{H}_2\text{S}$, $\text{H}_2\text{Se}$, $\text{H}_2\text{Te}$).



List I (Trend and Cause)List II (Property)
(A) Property that increases from $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ to $\text{H}_2\text{Te}$ due to decreasing bond dissociation enthalpy(I) Boiling point
(B) Property that decreases from $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ to $\text{H}_2\text{Te}$ due to decreasing bond dissociation enthalpy(II) Bond angle
(C) Property that decreases down the group due to decreasing electronegativity of the central atom(III) Acidic character
(D) Property that does not show a regular monotonic trend down the group(IV) Thermal stability


Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
Let us analyze each trend for the hydrides of Group 16 ($\text{H}_2\text{O}$, $\text{H}_2\text{S}$, $\text{H}_2\text{Se}$, $\text{H}_2\text{Te}$):



(A) Acidic character (III): Increases down the group from $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ to $\text{H}_2\text{Te}$. As the size of the central atom increases, the $\text{E}-\text{H}$ bond length increases and bond dissociation enthalpy decreases, making it easier to release an $\text{H}^+$ ion.



(B) Thermal stability (IV): Decreases down the group from $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ to $\text{H}_2\text{Te}$. This is also due to the decrease in $\text{E}-\text{H}$ bond dissociation enthalpy as the size of the central atom increases.



(C) Bond angle (II): Decreases down the group ($\text{H}_2\text{O} \gt \text{H}_2\text{S} \gt \text{H}_2\text{Se} \gt \text{H}_2\text{Te}$). As the electronegativity of the central atom decreases, the bond pairs of electrons are drawn further away from the central atom, decreasing the bond pair-bond pair repulsion and allowing the lone pairs to compress the bond angle more.



(D) Boiling point (I): Does not show a regular trend. $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ has an anomalously high boiling point due to extensive intermolecular hydrogen bonding. From $\text{H}_2\text{S}$ to $\text{H}_2\text{Te}$, the boiling point increases due to increasing van der Waals forces, making the overall order $\text{H}_2\text{S} \lt \text{H}_2\text{Se} \lt \text{H}_2\text{Te} \lt \text{H}_2\text{O}$.



Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(II), (D)-(I).



Answer: (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Read the following statements carefully:
(I) The maximum covalency of nitrogen is restricted to $4$.
(II) Nitrogen cannot form $d\pi$-$p\pi$ bonds with heavier elements.
(III) Nitrogen forms $p\pi$-$p\pi$ multiple bonds with itself.
(IV) Nitrogen has a higher tendency for catenation than phosphorus.

How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement (I) is correct. Nitrogen has only four orbitals (one 2s and three 2p) in its valence shell, so its maximum covalency is restricted to 4.

Statement (II) is correct. Due to the absence of vacant d-orbitals in its valence shell, nitrogen cannot form $d\pi$-$p\pi$ bonds.

Statement (III) is correct. Because of its small size and high electronegativity, nitrogen effectively forms strong $p\pi$-$p\pi$ multiple bonds with itself.

Statement (IV) is incorrect. The tendency for catenation depends on the strength of the single bond. The $\text{N}-\text{N}$ single bond is weaker than the $\text{P}-\text{P}$ single bond due to high interelectronic repulsion among the non-bonding electrons, owing to the small bond length. Thus, nitrogen has a weaker catenation tendency than phosphorus.

There are exactly 3 correct statements.

Answer: 3

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Graphite is the thermodynamically most stable allotrope of carbon, hence its standard enthalpy of formation is taken as zero.

Statement II: The high stability and electrical conductivity of graphite are due to the presence of delocalized $\pi$ electrons across its $\text{sp}^3$ hybridized planar sheets.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.solution:
Statement I is correct. Graphite is thermodynamically the most stable allotrope of carbon. Therefore, its standard enthalpy of formation ($\Delta_f H^{\ominus}$) is taken as zero.

Statement II is incorrect. While graphite does have delocalized $\pi$ electrons that account for its electrical conductivity, the carbon atoms in its planar sheets are $\text{sp}^2$ hybridized, not $\text{sp}^3$ hybridized. Diamond contains $\text{sp}^3$ hybridized carbon atoms.

Answer: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Phosphorus shows a much greater tendency for catenation than nitrogen.

Reason (R): The $\mathrm{N}-\mathrm{N}$ single bond is weaker than the $\mathrm{P}-\mathrm{P}$ single bond due to high interelectronic repulsion among non-bonding electrons.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is true: Phosphorus has a strong tendency for catenation (forming $\mathrm{P}_{4}$ molecules and polymeric chains), whereas nitrogen has a very limited tendency for catenation.

Reason (R) is true: The $\mathrm{N}-\mathrm{N}$ single bond is weaker than the $\mathrm{P}-\mathrm{P}$ single bond. This is because the small size of the nitrogen atom leads to high interelectronic repulsion between the non-bonding (lone pair) electrons on the adjacent atoms.

The extent of catenation depends directly on the strength of the element-element single bond. Since the $\mathrm{P}-\mathrm{P}$ single bond is stronger than the $\mathrm{N}-\mathrm{N}$ single bond, phosphorus shows a much greater tendency for catenation. Therefore, Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

Answer: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following pairs of molecules/ions have the same hybridization for their central atom, but different molecular geometries, and consist of one polar and one non-polar species?
questions.solution:
Let us analyze each pair based on VSEPR theory:

$\text{XeF}_4$ and $\text{XeOF}_4$:
In $\text{XeF}_4$, Xe has 4 bond pairs and 2 lone pairs ($\text{sp}^3\text{d}^2$ hybridization). Its geometry is square planar, which is highly symmetrical, making it non-polar.
In $\text{XeOF}_4$, Xe has 5 bond pairs (treating the double bond to O as one superpair for geometry) and 1 lone pair ($\text{sp}^3\text{d}^2$ hybridization). Its geometry is square pyramidal, which is asymmetrical, making it polar.
This pair has the same hybridization, different geometries, and one is polar while the other is non-polar.

$\text{XeF}_2$ and $\text{I}_3^-$:
Both have $\text{sp}^3\text{d}$ hybridization, 2 bond pairs, and 3 lone pairs. Both are linear and non-polar. (Fails criteria)

$\text{SF}_4$ and $\text{XeO}_2\text{F}_2$:
Both have $\text{sp}^3\text{d}$ hybridization, 4 bond pairs, and 1 lone pair. Both have a see-saw geometry and are polar. (Fails criteria)

$\text{PCl}_5$ and $\text{BrF}_5$:
$\text{PCl}_5$ is $\text{sp}^3\text{d}$ hybridized (trigonal bipyramidal, non-polar). $\text{BrF}_5$ is $\text{sp}^3\text{d}^2$ hybridized (square pyramidal, polar). They have different hybridizations. (Fails criteria)

Answer: $\text{XeF}_4$ and $\text{XeOF}_4$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Group 15 elements:
(A) The stability of hydrides decreases from $\text{NH}_3$ to $\text{BiH}_3$.
(B) The reducing character of hydrides decreases from $\text{NH}_3$ to $\text{BiH}_3$.
(C) All elements of Group 15 form $\text{E}_2\text{O}_5$ type oxides except nitrogen because it lacks d-orbitals.
(D) The acidic character of $\text{E}_2\text{O}_3$ oxides decreases down the group.

How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement (A) is correct: The stability of hydrides decreases down the group from $\text{NH}_3$ to $\text{BiH}_3$ because the E-H bond dissociation enthalpy decreases as atomic size increases.

Statement (B) is incorrect: The reducing character of hydrides increases down the group. Ammonia is a mild reducing agent while $\text{BiH}_3$ is the strongest reducing agent among them.

Statement (C) is incorrect: Nitrogen does form $\text{N}_2\text{O}_5$ despite lacking d-orbitals. It achieves a +5 oxidation state while maintaining a maximum covalency of 4 by forming p$\pi$-p$\pi$ multiple bonds.

Statement (D) is correct: The acidic character of oxides decreases down the group as the metallic character of the elements increases.

Therefore, only two statements, (A) and (D), are correct.

Answer: Only two

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Nitrogen exhibits a greater tendency for catenation compared to phosphorus.

Reason (R): The N-N single bond is weaker than the P-P single bond because of high interelectronic repulsion of the non-bonding electrons.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is false because the tendency of catenation in nitrogen is much less than that in phosphorus.

Reason (R) is true. Nitrogen has a small atomic size, which makes the N-N bond length very short. This leads to high interelectronic repulsion between the non-bonding electrons (lone pairs) on the adjacent nitrogen atoms.

As a result, the N-N single bond is weaker than the P-P single bond. This weak single bond is the very reason why nitrogen has a weaker catenation tendency.

Therefore, Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.

Answer: Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Addition of $\text{MnO}_2$ to a heated mixture of $\text{NaCl}$ and concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ changes the evolved gas from a greenish-yellow gas to a colourless, pungent-smelling gas.
Reason (R): In this reaction, $\text{MnO}_2$ acts as an oxidising agent and oxidises chloride ions to chlorine gas.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.solution:
Heating $\text{NaCl}$ with concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ alone produces hydrogen chloride ($\text{HCl}$) gas, which is a colourless, pungent-smelling gas:
$\text{NaCl} + \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 \rightarrow \text{NaHSO}_4 + \text{HCl}$

When $\text{MnO}_2$ is added to this mixture, it acts as an oxidising agent and oxidises the chloride ions to chlorine ($\text{Cl}_2$) gas, which is greenish-yellow in colour:
$2\text{NaCl} + \text{MnO}_2 + 2\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 \rightarrow \text{Na}_2\text{SO}_4 + \text{MnSO}_4 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{Cl}_2$

Thus, the addition of $\text{MnO}_2$ changes the evolved gas from a colourless, pungent-smelling gas ($\text{HCl}$) to a greenish-yellow gas ($\text{Cl}_2$). The Assertion states the reverse and is therefore incorrect.

The Reason correctly states that $\text{MnO}_2$ acts as an oxidising agent, oxidising chloride ions to chlorine gas.

Answer: (A) is incorrect but (R) is correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Compounds of the type $\mathrm{R_3P=O}$ (where $\mathrm{R}$ is an alkyl group) are known to exist, whereas the corresponding nitrogen analogues, $\mathrm{R_3N=O}$, do not. What is the primary underlying chemical reason for this observation?
options: Nitrogen is significantly more electronegative than phosphorus.
The $\mathrm{N-O}$ single bond is weaker than the $\mathrm{P-O}$ single bond due to interelectronic repulsions.
Nitrogen lacks valence $\mathrm{d}$-orbitals, restricting its maximum covalency to four and preventing $\mathrm{d\pi-p\pi}$ multiple bonding.
Nitrogen has a much higher ionization enthalpy than phosphorus.
questions.solution:
In the molecule $\mathrm{R_3P=O}$, phosphorus forms five bonds (covalency of 5) and utilizes its vacant $\mathrm{3d}$ orbital to form a $\mathrm{d\pi-p\pi}$ double bond with the $\mathrm{2p}$ orbital of oxygen.

Nitrogen belongs to the second period and has only $\mathrm{2s}$ and $\mathrm{2p}$ orbitals in its valence shell. Due to the absence of vacant $\mathrm{d}$-orbitals, nitrogen cannot expand its maximum covalency beyond four.

Furthermore, the lack of $\mathrm{d}$-orbitals means nitrogen cannot form $\mathrm{d\pi-p\pi}$ multiple bonds. Thus, a compound like $\mathrm{R_3N=O}$ with a true double bond and pentavalent nitrogen cannot exist. The other statements are true facts but do not explain this structural limitation.

Answer: Nitrogen lacks valence $\mathrm{d}$-orbitals, restricting its maximum covalency to four and preventing $\mathrm{d\pi-p\pi}$ multiple bonding.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the synthesis of ammonia via Haber's process:

Statement I: $1$ mole of $N_{2}$ reacts with $3$ moles of $H_{2}$ to give $2$ moles of $NH_{3}$.
Statement II: $22.4$ L of $N_{2}$ at STP reacts completely with $67.2$ L of $H_{2}$ at STP to give $44.8$ L of $NH_{3}$.
Statement III: $28$ g of $N_{2}$ reacts completely with $6$ g of $H_{2}$ to give $34$ g of $NH_{3}$.
Statement IV: If equal masses of $N_{2}$ and $H_{2}$ are taken, $N_{2}$ will act as the limiting reagent.

How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
The balanced chemical equation for Haber's process is:
$N_{2}(g) + 3H_{2}(g) \rightleftharpoons 2NH_{3}(g)$

Statement I is correct as the stoichiometric coefficients directly give the molar ratio: $1$ mole of $N_{2}$ reacts with $3$ moles of $H_{2}$ to produce $2$ moles of $NH_{3}$.

Statement II is correct because at STP, $1$ mole of any ideal gas occupies $22.4$ L. Thus, $1 \times 22.4$ L of $N_{2}$ reacts with $3 \times 22.4$ L ($67.2$ L) of $H_{2}$ to yield $2 \times 22.4$ L ($44.8$ L) of $NH_{3}$.

Statement III is correct as the molar mass of $N_{2}$ is $28$ g/mol, $H_{2}$ is $2$ g/mol, and $NH_{3}$ is $17$ g/mol. Therefore, $28$ g of $N_{2}$ reacts with $3 \times 2$ g ($6$ g) of $H_{2}$ to produce $2 \times 17$ g ($34$ g) of $NH_{3}$.

Statement IV is correct. If we take equal masses (e.g., $28$ g of each), we have $1$ mole of $N_{2}$ and $14$ moles of $H_{2}$. Since $1$ mole of $N_{2}$ requires only $3$ moles of $H_{2}$, $H_{2}$ is in excess and $N_{2}$ is the limiting reagent.

All four statements are correct.

Answer: $4$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The first step in the industrial preparation of nitric acid by the Ostwald process involves the catalytic oxidation of ammonia by atmospheric oxygen. What is the change in the oxidation state of nitrogen in this specific step?
questions.solution:
The first step of the Ostwald process is the catalytic oxidation of ammonia to nitric oxide:

$4\mathrm{NH}_3(\mathrm{g}) + 5\mathrm{O}_2(\mathrm{g}) \xrightarrow[\text{500 K, 9 bar}]{\text{Pt/Rh catalyst}} 4\mathrm{NO}(\mathrm{g}) + 6\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}(\mathrm{g})$

In ammonia ($\mathrm{NH}_3$), let the oxidation state of nitrogen be $x$.
$x + 3(+1) = 0 \Rightarrow x = -3$

In nitric oxide ($\mathrm{NO}$), let the oxidation state of nitrogen be $y$.
$y + (-2) = 0 \Rightarrow y = +2$

Therefore, the oxidation state of nitrogen changes from $-3$ to $+2$.

The option $-3 \text{ to } +4$ incorrectly assumes $\mathrm{NO}_2$ is the primary product of the first step, while $-3 \text{ to } +5$ incorrectly assumes $\mathrm{HNO}_3$ is formed directly.

Answer: $-3 \text{ to } +2$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Fluorine is a stronger oxidising agent than chlorine despite having a less negative electron gain enthalpy.

Reason (R): Fluorine does not exhibit any positive oxidation state in its compounds.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is true: Fluorine is the strongest oxidising agent among halogens. Its standard reduction potential is the highest, making it a stronger oxidising agent than chlorine, even though its electron gain enthalpy is less negative than that of chlorine.

Reason (R) is true: Fluorine is the most electronegative element and lacks vacant d-orbitals in its valence shell, so it exhibits only a -1 oxidation state and never a positive oxidation state.

However, Reason (R) does not explain Assertion (A). The correct explanation for the high oxidising power of fluorine is its low bond dissociation enthalpy and the high hydration enthalpy of the fluoride ion, which compensate for the less negative electron gain enthalpy.

Answer: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: When a black powder 'X' is heated with an alkali metal bromide and concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$, it yields a transition metal sulphate, an alkali metal sulphate, water, and a reddish-brown gas 'Z'. Identify 'X' and 'Z'.
questions.solution:
The reaction of an alkali metal bromide (such as $\text{NaBr}$) with concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ and manganese dioxide ($\text{MnO}_2$) produces bromine gas ($\text{Br}_2$).

The chemical equation is:
$2\text{NaBr} + \text{MnO}_2 + 2\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 \rightarrow \text{Na}_2\text{SO}_4 + \text{MnSO}_4 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{Br}_2$

In this reaction, $\text{MnO}_2$ is a black powder (X) that acts as an oxidising agent, oxidising bromide ions to bromine gas ($\text{Br}_2$), which is a reddish-brown gas (Z).

$\text{KMnO}_4$ is dark purple, not a black powder. $\text{CuO}$ does not oxidise bromides in this manner. $\text{NO}_2$ is reddish-brown but is evolved from nitrates, not bromides.

Answer: X = $\text{MnO}_2$, Z = $\text{Br}_2$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Graphite is soft and acts as a solid lubricant, whereas diamond is the hardest known natural substance.

Reason (R): Graphite has a 2D planar structure where layers are held together by weak van der Waals forces, while diamond has a rigid 3D network of $\text{sp}^{3}$ hybridized carbon atoms.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is NOT the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is correct: Graphite is soft and is used as a solid lubricant, whereas diamond is the hardest known natural substance.

Reason (R) is correct and explains the Assertion: In graphite, carbon atoms are $\text{sp}^{2}$ hybridized forming 2D planar hexagonal layers. These layers are held together by weak van der Waals forces, allowing them to slide over one another, which makes graphite soft and a good lubricant. In contrast, diamond has a rigid 3D network of $\text{sp}^{3}$ hybridized carbon atoms linked by strong directional covalent bonds, making it exceptionally hard.

Thus, both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

Answer: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Match the species in List-I with their characteristic bonding features in List-II.

List-IList-II
(A) $\text{N}_2$(I) $p\pi$-$p\pi$ multiple bond
(B) $\text{R}_3\text{P}=\text{CH}_2$(II) $d\pi$-$p\pi$ bond
(C) $\text{PR}_3$ complex with transition metals(III) $d\pi$-$d\pi$ bond
(D) $\text{P}_4$(IV) Only single bonds

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
Nitrogen lacks d-orbitals in its valence shell and its small size allows it to form strong $p\pi$-$p\pi$ multiple bonds. Thus, $\text{N}_2$ exists as a diatomic molecule with a triple bond.

Heavier elements like phosphorus have vacant d-orbitals. In compounds like $\text{R}_3\text{P}=\text{CH}_2$, phosphorus utilizes its d-orbitals to form a $d\pi$-$p\pi$ bond with carbon.

Phosphorus can also act as a $\pi$-acceptor ligand, forming $d\pi$-$d\pi$ back-bonds with the filled d-orbitals of transition metals in $\text{PR}_3$ complexes.

Due to their larger size and diffuse orbitals, heavier Group 15 elements do not form stable $p\pi$-$p\pi$ bonds. Consequently, phosphorus exists as a discrete tetrahedral $\text{P}_4$ molecule containing only single $\text{P}-\text{P}$ bonds.

Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(I), (B)-(II), (C)-(III), (D)-(IV).

Answer: (A)-(I), (B)-(II), (C)-(III), (D)-(IV)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In the industrial manufacture of nitric acid by the Ostwald process, the final chemical step involves the absorption of nitrogen dioxide gas in water to yield aqueous nitric acid. Which gaseous byproduct is generated during this absorption step, and what is its subsequent fate in the industrial plant?
options: $\mathrm{N_2O}$, which is released into the atmosphere
$\mathrm{NO_2}$, which is recycled back into the absorption tower
$\mathrm{NO}$, which is recycled and oxidized to $\mathrm{NO_2}$
questions.solution:
The third step of the Ostwald process is the absorption of nitrogen dioxide in water to form nitric acid. The balanced chemical equation for this step is:

$3\mathrm{NO_2}(\mathrm{g}) + \mathrm{H_2O}(\mathrm{l}) \rightarrow 2\mathrm{HNO_3}(\mathrm{aq}) + \mathrm{NO}(\mathrm{g})$

The gaseous byproduct generated is nitric oxide ($\mathrm{NO}$). In the industrial plant, this $\mathrm{NO}$ is not wasted; it is recycled back into the second step of the process where it is oxidized by air to form more $\mathrm{NO_2}$ ($2\mathrm{NO} + \mathrm{O_2} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{NO_2}$).

Answer: $\mathrm{NO}$, which is recycled and oxidized to $\mathrm{NO_2}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Very pure nitrogen gas can be obtained by heating barium azide.
Reason (R): The thermal decomposition of barium azide yields nitrogen gas and solid barium, leaving no other gaseous byproducts to contaminate the nitrogen.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is correct. Very pure nitrogen can be obtained by the thermal decomposition of sodium or barium azide.

Reason (R) is also correct and explains (A). The reaction is:
$Ba(N_3)_2 \rightarrow Ba(s) + 3N_2(g)$
Because barium is a solid metal, nitrogen is the only gaseous product formed. This absence of other gaseous byproducts is the reason why the nitrogen obtained is of very high purity.

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Both $\text{XeF}_4$ and $\text{SF}_4$ have the same molecular geometry because their central atoms are bonded to four fluorine atoms.
Reason (R): The central atom in $\text{XeF}_4$ is $sp^3d^2$ hybridized with two lone pairs, whereas the central atom in $\text{SF}_4$ is $sp^3d$ hybridized with one lone pair.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Assertion (A) is correct but Reason (R) is incorrect
Assertion (A) is incorrect but Reason (R) is correct
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is incorrect because $\text{XeF}_4$ and $\text{SF}_4$ have different molecular geometries. $\text{XeF}_4$ has a square planar geometry, while $\text{SF}_4$ has a see-saw geometry.

Reason (R) is correct. In $\text{XeF}_4$, Xenon has 8 valence electrons. Forming 4 single bonds with F leaves 4 non-bonding electrons (2 lone pairs). The steric number is $4 + 2 = 6$, corresponding to $sp^3d^2$ hybridization.

In $\text{SF}_4$, Sulphur has 6 valence electrons. Forming 4 single bonds with F leaves 2 non-bonding electrons (1 lone pair). The steric number is $4 + 1 = 5$, corresponding to $sp^3d$ hybridization.

Therefore, Assertion (A) is incorrect but Reason (R) is correct.

Answer: Assertion (A) is incorrect but Reason (R) is correct

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).



Assertion (A): The thermal stability of hydrogen halides decreases in the order $\text{HF} \gt \text{HCl} \gt \text{HBr} \gt \text{HI}$.



Reason (R): The acidic strength of hydrogen halides increases down the group from $\text{HF}$ to $\text{HI}$.



In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct.
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct.
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is correct: The thermal stability of hydrogen halides depends on their bond dissociation enthalpy. As the size of the halogen atom increases down the group, the $\text{H}-\text{X}$ bond length increases and the bond dissociation enthalpy decreases. Therefore, thermal stability decreases in the order $\text{HF} \gt \text{HCl} \gt \text{HBr} \gt \text{HI}$.



Reason (R) is correct: The acidic strength of hydrides depends on the ease of losing an $\text{H}^+$ ion, which in turn depends on the bond dissociation enthalpy. Since the $\text{H}-\text{X}$ bond becomes weaker down the group, acidic strength increases from $\text{HF}$ to $\text{HI}$.



Conclusion: Both statements are correct, but they are independent consequences of the same underlying cause (decreasing bond dissociation enthalpy down the group). The increasing acidic strength does not explain the decreasing thermal stability. Hence, (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).



Answer: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the properties of Group 17 elements and their compounds:

(A)Acidic strength of $\mathrm{HX}$(I)$\mathrm{Cl_2} \gt \mathrm{Br_2} \gt \mathrm{F_2} \gt \mathrm{I_2}$
(B)Bond dissociation enthalpy of $\mathrm{X_2}$(II)$\mathrm{Cl} \gt \mathrm{F} \gt \mathrm{Br} \gt \mathrm{I}$
(C)Negative electron gain enthalpy of $\mathrm{X}$(III)$\mathrm{HI} \gt \mathrm{HBr} \gt \mathrm{HCl} \gt \mathrm{HF}$
(D)Oxidising power of $\mathrm{X_2}$(IV)$\mathrm{F_2} \gt \mathrm{Cl_2} \gt \mathrm{Br_2} \gt \mathrm{I_2}$


Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
(A) Acidic strength of $\mathrm{HX}$: The acidic strength increases down the group as the size of the halogen atom increases, which decreases the $\mathrm{H-X}$ bond dissociation enthalpy. Order: $\mathrm{HI} \gt \mathrm{HBr} \gt \mathrm{HCl} \gt \mathrm{HF}$.

(B) Bond dissociation enthalpy of $\mathrm{X_2}$: Fluorine has an anomalously low bond dissociation enthalpy due to strong interelectronic repulsions between the lone pairs on the small fluorine atoms. Order: $\mathrm{Cl_2} \gt \mathrm{Br_2} \gt \mathrm{F_2} \gt \mathrm{I_2}$.

(C) Negative electron gain enthalpy of $\mathrm{X}$: Chlorine has a more negative electron gain enthalpy than fluorine because of the small size of the fluorine atom, which causes strong interelectronic repulsions in its relatively compact 2p subshell. Order: $\mathrm{Cl} \gt \mathrm{F} \gt \mathrm{Br} \gt \mathrm{I}$.

(D) Oxidising power of $\mathrm{X_2}$: Fluorine is the strongest oxidising agent due to its low bond dissociation enthalpy and high hydration enthalpy of the $\mathrm{F^-}$ ion. Order: $\mathrm{F_2} \gt \mathrm{Cl_2} \gt \mathrm{Br_2} \gt \mathrm{I_2}$.

Answer: (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(II), (D)-(IV)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following correctly represents the order of acidic strength of Group 16 hydrides and the primary reason for this trend?
options: $H_2O \gt  H_2S \gt  H_2Se \gt  H_2Te$ ; Reason: Decrease in electronegativity of the central atom down the group.
$H_2O \lt  H_2S \lt  H_2Se \lt  H_2Te$ ; Reason: Increase in electronegativity of the central atom down the group.
$H_2O \gt  H_2S \gt  H_2Se \gt  H_2Te$ ; Reason: Presence of strong intermolecular hydrogen bonding in $H_2O$.
$H_2O \lt  H_2S \lt  H_2Se \lt  H_2Te$ ; Reason: Decrease in H-E bond dissociation enthalpy down the group.
questions.solution:
Down Group 16, as the atomic size of the central atom (E) increases, the H-E bond length increases.

This leads to a decrease in the H-E bond dissociation enthalpy down the group.

Because the bond becomes weaker and easier to break, the release of $H^+$ ions becomes progressively easier.

Therefore, the acidic strength increases in the order $H_2O \lt H_2S \lt H_2Se \lt H_2Te$.

Answer: $H_2O \lt H_2S \lt H_2Se \lt H_2Te$ ; Reason: Decrease in H-E bond dissociation enthalpy down the group.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-IList-II
(A) Diamond(I) $\text{sp}^2$ hybridized, pure form without dangling bonds
(B) Graphite(II) $\text{sp}^3$ hybridized, rigid 3D network
(C) Fullerene(III) $\text{sp}^2$ hybridized, layered structure with van der Waals forces
(D) Carbon black(IV) Amorphous form obtained by burning hydrocarbons in limited supply of air

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
Diamond has a rigid 3D network of $\text{sp}^3$ hybridized carbon atoms.

Graphite has a layered structure where each layer consists of planar hexagonal rings of $\text{sp}^2$ hybridized carbon atoms, and the layers are held together by weak van der Waals forces.

Fullerenes are the purest form of carbon because they have smooth structure without dangling bonds, and their carbon atoms are $\text{sp}^2$ hybridized.

Carbon black is an amorphous form of carbon obtained by burning hydrocarbons in a limited supply of air.

Answer: (A) - (II), (B) - (III), (C) - (I), (D) - (IV)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the number of moles of ammonia produced when $56\text{ g}$ of nitrogen gas reacts completely with excess hydrogen gas in Haber's process?
questions.solution:
The balanced chemical equation for Haber's process is:

$\text{N}_{2}(\text{g}) + 3\text{H}_{2}(\text{g}) \rightleftharpoons 2\text{NH}_{3}(\text{g})$

First, calculate the number of moles of nitrogen gas ($\text{N}_{2}$):
Molar mass of $\text{N}_{2} = 28\text{ g mol}^{-1}$
Moles of $\text{N}_{2} = \dfrac{56\text{ g}}{28\text{ g mol}^{-1}} = 2\text{ moles}$

According to the stoichiometry of the reaction, $1\text{ mole}$ of $\text{N}_{2}$ produces $2\text{ moles}$ of $\text{NH}_{3}$.
Therefore, $2\text{ moles}$ of $\text{N}_{2}$ will produce $2 \times 2 = 4\text{ moles}$ of $\text{NH}_{3}$.

Answer: $4$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A halogen 'X' forms only one oxoacid and does not exhibit any positive oxidation states. Furthermore, it reacts readily with water to produce oxygen gas. Identify the halogen 'X' and the primary reason it cannot exhibit positive oxidation states like $+3, +5$, and $+7$.
options: Chlorine; absence of vacant d-orbitals in its valence shell
Fluorine; anomalously low bond dissociation enthalpy
Bromine; high electronegativity and large atomic size
Fluorine; absence of vacant d-orbitals in its valence shell
questions.solution:
The halogen 'X' is fluorine. Fluorine is the most electronegative element and reacts with water to oxidize it to oxygen gas. It forms only one oxoacid, $\mathrm{HOF}$ (hypofluorous acid).

Unlike other halogens (chlorine, bromine, and iodine) which can expand their octet to show $+3, +5$, and $+7$ oxidation states, fluorine is restricted to a $-1$ oxidation state. This restriction is primarily due to the absence of vacant d-orbitals in its valence shell, which prevents the promotion of electrons and expansion of its covalency.

While fluorine does have a low bond dissociation enthalpy, this explains its high reactivity as an oxidizing agent, not its restricted oxidation states.

Answer: Fluorine; absence of vacant d-orbitals in its valence shell

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the hydrides of Group 17 elements:

(a) The acidic strength increases in the order $HF \lt HCl \lt HBr \lt HI$.
(b) The reducing character increases from $HF$ to $HI$.
(c) The trends in both acidic strength and reducing character are primarily due to the decrease in H-X bond dissociation enthalpy down the group.
(d) $HF$ is the strongest reducing agent among the hydrogen halides due to the high electronegativity of fluorine.

How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement (a) is correct: Acidic strength of Group 17 hydrides increases down the group ($HF \lt HCl \lt HBr \lt HI$) because the release of a proton becomes easier.

Statement (b) is correct: The reducing character depends on the ease of releasing hydrogen, which increases down the group from $HF$ to $HI$.

Statement (c) is correct: As atomic size increases down the group, the H-X bond length increases and the bond dissociation enthalpy decreases. This weaker bond is the primary reason for both the increasing acidic strength and the increasing reducing character.

Statement (d) is incorrect: $HI$ is the strongest reducing agent among the hydrogen halides, not $HF$. The high electronegativity and small size of fluorine make the H-F bond very strong, making $HF$ the weakest reducing agent.

Therefore, exactly three statements are correct.

Answer: Three

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Match List I with List II.

List IList II
(A) $\mathrm{N_2}$ molecule(I) Single bonds only
(B) $\mathrm{P_4}$ molecule(II) $\mathrm{p\pi-p\pi}$ multiple bonding
(C) $\mathrm{R_3P=O}$ molecule(III) $\mathrm{d\pi-p\pi}$ multiple bonding
(D) Transition metal complex with $\mathrm{PEt_3}$(IV) $\mathrm{d\pi-d\pi}$ backbonding

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
Nitrogen ($\mathrm{N}$) is a small atom and forms strong $\mathrm{p\pi-p\pi}$ multiple bonds with itself, resulting in the $\mathrm{N \equiv N}$ triple bond in the $\mathrm{N_2}$ molecule. (A matches II)

Phosphorus ($\mathrm{P}$) is larger and does not effectively form $\mathrm{p\pi-p\pi}$ bonds. Instead, it undergoes catenation through $\mathrm{P-P}$ single bonds, forming the tetrahedral $\mathrm{P_4}$ molecule. (B matches I)

In $\mathrm{R_3P=O}$, phosphorus uses its vacant $\mathrm{3d}$ orbital to overlap with the $\mathrm{2p}$ orbital of oxygen, forming a $\mathrm{d\pi-p\pi}$ double bond. (C matches III)

Heavier elements like phosphorus and arsenic can act as ligands (e.g., $\mathrm{PEt_3}$, $\mathrm{AsPh_3}$) and accept electron density from the filled $\mathrm{d}$-orbitals of transition metals into their own empty $\mathrm{d}$-orbitals, forming $\mathrm{d\pi-d\pi}$ backbonds. (D matches IV)

Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(II), (B)-(I), (C)-(III), (D)-(IV).

Answer: (A)-(II), (B)-(I), (C)-(III), (D)-(IV)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following statements regarding Group 15 elements and their compounds is incorrect?
options: $\mathrm{BiF_5}$ is the only stable pentahalide of bismuth.
The covalency of nitrogen in $\mathrm{N_2O_5}$ is 5.
$\mathrm{PH_3}$ has a lower boiling point than $\mathrm{NH_3}$.
$\mathrm{Sb_2O_3}$ is amphoteric in nature while $\mathrm{P_2O_3}$ is acidic.
questions.solution:
Statement 1 is correct: Due to the strong inert pair effect, the +5 oxidation state of bismuth is highly unstable. However, $\mathrm{BiF_5}$ exists as the only stable pentahalide because of the small size and high electronegativity of fluorine.

Statement 2 is incorrect: The maximum covalency of nitrogen is restricted to 4 because it lacks d-orbitals in its valence shell. In $\mathrm{N_2O_5}$, the oxidation state of nitrogen is +5, but its covalency is 4.

Statement 3 is correct: $\mathrm{NH_3}$ has a higher boiling point than $\mathrm{PH_3}$ because ammonia molecules are associated through intermolecular hydrogen bonding, which is absent in phosphine.

Statement 4 is correct: The acidic character of Group 15 oxides decreases down the group. Oxides of nitrogen and phosphorus (like $\mathrm{P_2O_3}$) are acidic, arsenic and antimony (like $\mathrm{Sb_2O_3}$) are amphoteric, and bismuth is predominantly basic.

Answer: The covalency of nitrogen in $\mathrm{N_2O_5}$ is 5.

Assertion : $\mathrm{HClO}_4$ is a stronger acid than $\mathrm{HClO}_3$.
Reason : Oxidation state of $\mathrm{Cl}$ in $\mathrm{HClO}_4$ is +8 and in $\mathrm{HClO}_3+5$.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false.
questions.solution:
Greater the number of negative atoms present in the oxy-acid make the acid stronger.
In general, the strengths of acids that have general formula, $(\mathrm{HO})_m \mathrm{ZO}_n$ can be related to the value of $n$. As the value of $n$ increases, acidic character also increases. The negative atoms draw electrons away from the Z-atom and make it more positive. The Zatom, therefore, becomes more effective in withdrawing electron density away from the oxygen atom that bonded to hydrogen. In turn, the electrons of $\mathrm{H}-\mathrm{O}$ bond are drawn more strongly away from the $H$-atom. The net effect makes it easier from the proton release and increases the acid strength.

options: Boiling point increases with increasing atomic mass
Helium has least tendency to form compound
Noble gases have some value of electron affinity
Xenon has maximum number of compounds
questions.solution:
(1) Intermolecular van der Waals' force exists between atoms of noble gases. The magnitude of these forces increases with increasing atomic mass which directly related to boiling point.
(2) As ionisation energy of helium is maximum, thus, electrons are lightly held to the nucleus and therefore has least tendency to form compound.
(3) As valence shells of noble gases are complete, thus they do not show tendency to gain electrons. Therefore, they have zero electron affinity.
(4) As Xenon has lowest ionisation energy, they have maximum number of compounds.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which will liberate bromine from a solution of potassium bromide?
questions.solution:
Since, $E^{\circ}$ of $\mathrm{Cl}_2$ is higher than that of $\mathrm{Br}_2$, therefore $\mathrm{Cl}_2$ has a higher tendency to accept electrons than $\mathrm{Br}_2$. Conversely, $\mathrm{Br}^{-}$ion has a higher tendency to lose electrons than $\mathrm{Cl}^{-}$ion. Therefore, the following reaction will occur
$\mathrm{KBr} \longrightarrow \mathrm{K}^{+}+\mathrm{Br}^{-}2 \mathrm{Br}^{-}+\mathrm{Cl}_2 \longrightarrow 2 \mathrm{Cl}^{-}+\mathrm{Br}_2$
Thus, $\mathrm{Br}^{-}$ions are oxidised to $\mathrm{Br}_2$ by $\mathrm{Cl}_2$, which itself is reduced to $\mathrm{Cl}^{-}$ions.
